questions.stem: A goat is tied to a post by a rope of length 4 m. What is the shape of the locus of points the goat can reach?
questions.explanation: The goat can reach any point up to 4 m from the post in all directions. This is a circle with radius 4 m centred on the post.

questions.stem: What is the locus of points equidistant from two fixed points A and B?

options.text: A circle passing through A and B

questions.explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equidistant from A and B. This is the definition of the perpendicular bisector.

questions.stem: What is the locus of points equidistant from two intersecting lines?

options.text: A circle centred at the intersection
The perpendicular bisector of each line
The angle bisectors of the angles formed by the two lines
A straight line parallel to both

questions.explanation: The locus of points equidistant from two intersecting lines consists of the angle bisectors of the angles formed by the lines. There are two such bisectors, perpendicular to each other.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 10 m by 6 m. A tree must be planted more than 2 m from every edge. What is the area of the region where the tree can be planted?
questions.explanation: The tree must be more than 2 m from each edge, so the available region is a smaller rectangle: (10 - 2 - 2) by (6 - 2 - 2) = 6 m by 2 m = 12 m squared.

questions.stem: A point P moves so that it is always exactly 3 cm from a fixed straight line L. What is the locus of P?

options.text: A single straight line parallel to L
Two straight lines, each 3 cm from L, one on each side

questions.explanation: Points exactly 3 cm from a straight line form two parallel lines, one on each side of L, each 3 cm from L.
